title: admin-activity-visualizer-heatmap-and-provision-wizard-notes
content:
TL;DR: sketch for an Admin Activity Visualizer — a combined timeline + heatmap view to help org admins and security leads understand spikes in key events (API key creation, service-account issuance, role changes) and then act (bulk rotate, revoke, escalate). Also a lightweight provisioning wizard for creating bounded service accounts with recommended RBAC templates. Draft UX, wireframe notes, edge cases, and backlog items below.

Goals (product):
- Surface anomalous admin activity quickly without leaving org settings.
- Make bulk mitigations (rotate keys, revoke tokens, disable service accounts) safe and auditable.
- Reduce context-switching to Observability; let admins triage then drill into raw audit logs.
- Provide a simple provisioning flow for service accounts that enforces least privilege with templates.

Primary personas:
- Org admin (security-first, needs quick triage)
- Engineering manager (wants assurance on team keys and service account usage)
- Platform/security analyst (wants exportable CSVs and links to full raw logs)

Key metrics to monitor (for success/future A/B):
- Time from alert -> first mitigation click (target < 5 min for high-severity events)
- Fraction of bulk rotations completed without follow-up support ticket (> 85%)
- Reduction in orphaned API keys over 90d window

Overview of components (UI pieces):
1) Top strip: quick summary chips
   - total admin events (24h), high-severity events, keys created, keys rotated, SA created
   - quick filters: timeframe (1h / 24h / 7d / custom), severity (info/warn/critical), resource-type (api_key/sa/role)

2) Activity heatmap (visual):
   - X-axis: time (granularity auto-adjusts: minutes -> hours -> days)
   - Y-axis: event type groups (API keys, Service accounts, RBAC changes, Login failures)
   - color intensity = event count normalized per-type; hover shows top 3 events for that cell
   - click on a cell opens a compact timeline below with relevant items pre-filtered
   - keyboard accessible: arrow keys move focus across heatmap cells

3) Compact timeline (list) below heatmap
   - each item: icon, timestamp, user (name + email), resource, brief description, quick actions (investigate, revoke, rotate, open raw log)
   - pagination + load more; infinite scroll for broad ranges
   - inline expansion to show raw JSON snippet from audit log (collapsible)

4) Bulk Action bar (contextual, sticky)
   - appears when items selected (checkboxes) or when heatmap cell selected -> select all in query
   - actions: rotate API keys, revoke tokens, disable SAs, assign temporary role, export CSV
   - secondary actions: create support ticket, notify owner (email / Slack)
   - safety: require typed confirmation for high-impact ops (e.g., "ROTATE 12 KEYS") and show preflight summary of affected services (best-effort mapping)

5) Provisioning wizard for new service accounts (side rail modal)
   - Step 1: name, description, owner (team), allowed uses (embed, inference, background job)
   - Step 2: RBAC recommendation (3 curated templates: read-only, inference-runner, infra-admin). Each template shows recommended policies and potential downstream resources impacted. Template preview shows explicit permitted API calls and example least-privilege IAM assertion.
   - Step 3: key lifetime / rotation policy (recommended 30d, option to auto-rotate) + KMS scope
   - Step 4: summary + create. On create, produce a verifiable artifact: short-lived key + download link + rotation cron stub in infra repo (optional GitHub PR template).

Wireframe sketch (very rough):
[HEADER chips]
|------------------------------|
| Heatmap (left) | Timeline (right) |
| Heatmap grid    | Item list       |
|                Bulk action bar (sticky)      |
| Provision modal (on create)                   |

Interaction scenarios (examples):
- Scenario A: Security analyst sees a midday spike in API-key creations for "payments" service. They click the heatmap cell -> timeline shows 9 keys created in 15m. Select all -> run "rotate keys" bulk action with typed confirmation. After action, auto-insert ticket in support queue + post summary to #security-ops.
- Scenario B: Team lead wants to provision a new SA that only runs embeddings. Uses provisioning wizard, picks "inference-runner" template, auto-rotate policy set to 14d. On create, an ephemeral key is returned and a GitHub PR template is offered to add rotation cron to infra.

Edge cases / unresolved UX questions:
- How to map "affected services" when keys are used by many ephemeral jobs? (we can show recent top 10 consumer IPs / user agents as a heuristic)
- RBAC preview: do we compute a dry-run of effective permissions across org? Potentially expensive; consider cached last-known effective-role-snapshot and a freshness indicator.
- Bulk rotate rollback story (if a rotation breaks prod). Need fast undo: re-issue previous key or provide automated fallbacks (keep old key valid for short TTL). Operational complexity requires SRE sign-off.
- Audit compliance: every bulk action must create an immutable audit record with who executed, what query was targeted, and the preflight diff. Consider a downloadable signed artifact for compliance teams.

Accessibility notes:
- Heatmap should not rely on color alone; provide numeric labels and an alternate condensed text table.
- Keyboard-first navigation for timeline and bulk actions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Heatmap + timeline loads < 800ms for 24h window for orgs with < 100k events/day (backend SLA)
- Bulk rotate API keys action implements typed confirmation, audit record, and a safety TTL for old key (configurable)
- Provisioning wizard implements templates + returns an ephemeral key download.
- Export CSV and link-to-raw-log present for each timeline item

Backlog (stories + rough estimates):
- CON-7842: Heatmap rendering component + backend aggregation API (3w)
- CON-7843: Timeline list + inline raw JSON (2w)
- CON-7844: Bulk actions infra + UI (rotate/revoke) + audit artifact (4w)
- CON-7845: Provisioning wizard + templates + key issuance (3w)
- CON-7846: Permissions dry-run/cached snapshots (research spike 1w)

Notes for engineering:
- Backend: aggregation job should precompute heatmap buckets for typical windows (1h, 24h, 7d) and store freshness metadata. Use existing audit log indexer (observability team) to avoid duplicate ingestion.
- Security: rotating keys must call KMS + record old key fingerprint; ensure rotation is atomic from the app's perspective or present a short TTL fallback toggle.
- Frontend: make heatmap canvas-based to handle dense events; timeline is virtualized list. Provide API that supports both cell drilldown and freeform filter queries.

Next steps / owners:
- Design: Aisha to produce high-fidelity heatmap + timeline mocks (due 2026-02-28)
- Eng spike: Ravi to prototype aggregation pipeline and run on a sampled org dump (due 2026-03-07)
- Security review: Jonah to list compliance requirements for bulk-op artifacts (due 2026-03-03)

Open questions for PM review:
- Do we enable auto-rotation as default for new SAs? (pros: security; cons: developer friction)
- What is the default retention window surfaced in the heatmap? 90 days vs 365 days.

Related doc refs:
- role-templates-service-account-creation-flow-notes (see templates mapping)
- service-account-usage-metering-and-rotation-flow-draft (rotation safety patterns)

Notes-to-self: keep the initial feature set narrow. MVP = visibility + one safe mitigation (rotate/revoke) + provisioning with constrained templates. Avoid trying to fully compute effective permissions in first iteration.

End of draft.
